label: Women
why: Bordeaux — the couture house red, of the carpet and the box. Not pink.

label: Men
why: Indigo — tailoring navy and denim. Not blue-for-boys.

label: Curve
why: Terracotta — warm and declarative. The board fought for its place; it should not read apologetic.

label: Petite
why: Dusty rose — adjacent to Women, lower in arousal.

label: Kids & Teens
why: Deep sage, held low in chroma so the board never reads playful or marketable. Note this is a tone decision, not a safeguarding control — real safeguarding is guardian consent and visibility gating, not a saturation value.

label: Classic
why: Bronze-taupe — patina. Age as an asset, not a fade.

label: Talent
why: Plum-grey — stage curtain, house lights down.

label: New Faces
why: Fresh olive — growth, unripe, not yet arrived.

label: Development
why: Raw sienna — earth and work-in-progress. Raw material being worked.

label: Main Board
why: Warm amber — quiet, but no longer near-grey. At C 0.016 the flagship board was indistinguishable from Unassigned, so the most important board on a roster read as a data gap.

label: Editorial
why: Restrained violet-ink. Editorial identity leans on the absence of colour — Vogue runs monochrome and lets the image carry it — so this is the quietest market board, though not achromatic: pure grey collapses under CVD.

label: Commercial
why: Trust blue — the most reliably "competent/dependable" hue cross-culturally. Commercial is the workhorse board.

label: Runway
why: Bronze — show invitations are foil-stamped. Ceremony and occasion.

label: Beauty
why: Rose — beauty packaging documentably moved from clinical white to rose quartz and blush. Skin, intimacy, care.

label: Digital
why: Cyan-teal — screen-native signal. Held bright rather than dark; dark low-chroma cyan is the region cross-cultural work associates with negative affect.

label: Lifestyle
why: Moss — domestic, outdoors, real people.

label: Fitness
why: Electric blue — activewear trades in kinetic brights and dopamine colour. The highest-arousal division in the industry gets the highest chroma in the palette.

label: Swim
why: Aqua — the 2026 trade reports name blue "the new neutral" for swim.

label: Fit
why: Steel — instrument grey-blue. Fit is booked on measurement, not on look, and the colour should be as unglamorous as the job.

label: Parts
why: Mauve-grey — clinical and close-up.

label: Artists
why: Warm stone — hands, craft, materials.

label: Unassigned
why: True neutral. No board, no hue.
